events.note: L-4 cab with catwalk on a 20 ft H-braced steel tower (NHLR; fire-lookouts.org). Peakbagging says the CCC built it.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register April 21, 1999 (US 302, CA 30). Nominated by Mark Swift.
Peakbagging photos taken August 11, 2008 show a lookout at the Osborne fire finder.
FFLA $500 restoration grant to the Buck Rock Foundation for the Forest Service rehabilitation; foundation matched with $500. Work on windows, frames, siding and shutters.
External and internal painting of the cab completed.
New shutter system, plumbing and electrical work for tower safety, mostly by Buck Rock Foundation volunteers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR says one of only 20 L-4 cabs remaining in California; fire-lookouts.org says one of only 18. The story reports both figures.
NHLR gives 5,231 ft (1,594 m), which matches the record's 1594.4 m. Peakbagging gives 5256 ft. The record was kept, and the story gives no elevation.
Only Peakbagging names the CCC as builder. NHLR and fire-lookouts.org give the 1934 date without naming a builder. The story attributes the CCC claim to Peakbagging.

notes_for_editor: The record's 1934 build date, 1999 registration and 1594.4 m elevation match the NHLR, so no correction is proposed. The record's coordinates match fire-lookouts.org. Sources disagree on the L-4 cab count (20 vs 18) and on elevation (5,231 ft vs 5,256 ft). The CCC attribution rests only on Peakbagging. Staffing and active-service claims come from pages last updated in 2013; no 2026 confirmation was found, and the access level 'restricted' is a judgment. The fire-lookouts.org/cali/fence_meadow/ variant returned the same text, so it was not counted as a separate source. Story is about 330 words including footnotes.
